The product spawns the stand-in with the real command line; its argv, working directory, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and every request it receives (health check, /props, chat) are the recorded launches and requests (the OpenAI SDK sends real HTTP to it; it answers 400 if a system message is not first). Not run here: Apple Silicon (a darwin host: native sysctl and the machine's own RAM and CPU name decide the GPU and its launch arguments).
exclusions: launches and requests of the stand-in llama-server (the case result `launches` and the row `requests`): the loopback port (random) is written as <port> in argv after --port, in the Host header and in origin; the API key (random, 32 bytes hex, minted by the product per start) is written as <api-key> in argv after --api-key and in the Authorization header, with the stand-in's own check `authorized` (the bearer key it was started with matched) recorded beside it; the data directory is written as <data> in argv (--model) and cwd, with forward slashes; every other argument and header is recorded and compared as it arrived

the stand-in answers the health check once per start: the product polls /health until the first answer, a refused connection never reaches the stand-in, so the one health request it received is the whole health record

Apple Silicon is not recorded: the launch arguments on that platform (GPU uuid MTL0, memory from the host's RAM and CPU name via native os calls) depend on the host; the NVIDIA kinds (none via failing query, none via empty listing, insufficient free memory, one GPU, two GPUs) are recorded

no string is rewritten: the data directory is the fixed D:/mixdog-build/tmp/w22/<set> and the product tree D:/mixdog-build/tmp/b6f-tree (paths as Node produced them, Windows separators where Node wrote them): a replay maps its own temp directory to that prefix

net requests: the VALUES of the request headers x-stainless-os, x-stainless-arch and x-stainless-runtime-version (the SDK client stack writes the recording host's OS, architecture and Node version) are replaced by the marker `<recording host <header name>>` at exactly those header names; every other header is recorded and compared as it arrived
net requests: the recorder's x-bench-origin header is left out and `host` is the host of the origin the product addressed (the loopback port is random)
